violations.why: measure3 (prio 6) can preempt measure2 between its write and the read and change tickCounter, so the check sees a different value.
communicate (prio 3) preempts measure2 (prio 2) between the write and the read and rewrites tickCounter.
measure3 (prio 6) preempts measure1 and increments numberOfRecords after it was used as the index, so the later increment reads a changed value.
measure3 changes numberOfRecords between the index read and the increment write, which makes the record slot stale and loses an update.
The non-atomic increment in measure1 can be preempted by measure3's increment, and one update is lost.
measure1 (prio 5) preempts communicate (prio 3) between its read of numberOfRecords and its reset to 0, so the overflow check uses a stale value.
measure3 (prio 6) preempts communicate between its read of numberOfRecords and its reset, so the overflow check uses a stale value.
